section.question: This page got slow as accounts grew. What is wrong with it, and how would you fix it?
section.snippet: class OrdersController < ApplicationController def index @orders = current_account.orders.order(created_at: :desc).limit(50) end end # app/views/orders/index.html.erb <% @orders.each do |order| %> <%= order.number %> <%= order.customer.name %> <% end %>

answers.complete: Each row calls order.customer, and nothing loaded the customers, so Rails runs one query for the orders and then one more per row: up to 51 queries for 50 orders. That is an N+1, and it grows with the page size. Preload the customers in the controller: current_account.orders.includes(:customer).order(created_at: :desc).limit(50). Then it is two queries however many rows there are.
answers.partial: The view calls order.customer for every row, which runs a separate query each time, an N+1. That is why the page slows down as there are more orders.
answers.miss: Fifty rows is too many for one page. I would paginate to 20 per page and add an index on orders.created_at so the sort is faster.
